key_insight: Cross-lingual factual inconsistency in LLMs can often be reduced at inference time, with simple persona prompting outperforming more invasive intervention methods in robustness and transfer.
engineering_relevance: For multilingual deployments, inference-time steering offers a practical, low-risk way to improve language-consistent answers without retraining or permanently altering the model.
method: Zero-shot persona prompting to make an English-prompted model respond as if queried in German, Spanish, or Bulgarian.
Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) to manipulate internal representations at inference time.
Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) adapters trained on factual and conceptual generalization data for lightweight weight updates.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates interventions on a multilingual factual dataset and a new culturally rooted generalization benchmark using Gemma 3 12B Instruct.
watch_item: CAA and DPO can improve consistency but may be configuration-sensitive, less transferable, or cause knowledge degradation outside the target setting.
paper_title: Inference-Time Steering for Cross-Lingual Factual Consistency in LLMs
